summary: Despite Georgia's reputation for strict exotic-pet laws, the roof rat is explicitly carved out: the state's Wild Animal license rule (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. r. 391-4-8-.05) lists the rodent order as 'all species except … Rattus rattus …,' naming the roof rat among the species that need NO Wild Animal License. So you can legally keep, breed, and give away a captive-bred roof rat with no DNR license, and pet rodents are exempt from Georgia's import veterinary-certificate (CVI) rule. The only caveat is commercial scale: selling more than 30 self-raised animals a year (or running a business) requires a Georgia Dept of Agriculture pet-dealer license.

keep.why: Georgia's Wild Animal license requirement (O.C.G.A. §27-5-5) applies only to species the Board of Natural Resources lists by rule. Rule 391-4-8-.05's Order Rodentia entry reads 'All species except … Rattus rattus …,' naming the roof/black rat among the species that do NOT require a Wild Animal License. So no DNR license or permit is needed to keep one as a pet. Gemini DR-verified: R. rattus is named in the Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 391-4-8-.05 wildlife-license exemption (alongside R. norvegicus) -> treated as a standard pet by the GDA, not regulated wildlife.
keep.governing_law: Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. r. 391-4-8-.05 (Order Rodentia exemption naming R. rattus); O.C.G.A. §27-5-4 & §27-5-5.

breed.why: There is no separate breeding permit for an exempt rodent, if keeping is unlicensed, hobby breeding is likewise unregulated by DNR (R. rattus is off the regulated wild-animal list). The only breeding-adjacent touchpoint is the Dept of Agriculture pet-dealer threshold, which governs commercial selling, not breeding itself. Gemini DR-verified: hobby breeding is free only up to the GDA Pet Dealer threshold - selling/exchanging/adopting-out >1 litter OR >30 adults per 12 months requires a GDA Pet Dealer License (40-13-13-.07); 'giving away' counts as 'offers for adoption.'
breed.governing_law: Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. r. 391-4-8-.05; (commercial overlay) O.C.G.A. §4-11-2 & §4-11-3.

sell_give.why: DNR places no sale restriction on R. rattus (it is exempt from the wild-animal list). But the Georgia Animal Protection Act defines 'pet' to include 'rodent,' so selling above the statutory threshold makes you a 'pet dealer' needing a Dept of Agriculture license: the exemption covers a person who 'sells only animals that he or she has produced and raised, not to exceed 30 animals a year' and isn't otherwise a licensed business. Casual sale/giving below that threshold needs no license. Gemini DR-verified: a GDA Pet Dealer License is required above the >1-litter / >30-adult hobbyist exemption; rodents are exempt from outgoing sales-record keeping.

transport.why: Georgia's import Certificate of Veterinary Inspection (CVI) requirement covers 'all pets except fish and rodents,' so rodents, including R. rattus, are exempt from the import CVI. No state import permit or health certificate is required for a pet roof rat. (Federal USFWS Form 3-177 still applies to international movement, see United States.) Gemini DR-verified: rodents are exempt from the CVI requirement for pets entering Georgia (40-13-2-.19(4)); intrastate unrestricted. (Federal: international import = USFWS Form 3-177 + CDC African-rodent embargo.)
transport.governing_law: Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. ch. 40-13-2 (interstate movement / CVI); GA Dept of Agriculture 'Bringing Animals into Georgia.'

restrictions.summary: Selling more than 30 self-raised animals per year, or operating as a business, makes you a 'pet dealer' under the Georgia Animal Protection Act and requires a Dept of Agriculture pet-dealer license. Private, low-volume placement and giveaways are exempt.
steps: Stay under 30 self-raised animals/year to remain exempt, or apply for a GA Dept of Agriculture pet-dealer license
restrictions.where_to_file: Georgia Dept of Agriculture (Companion Animal/Equine Division)

restrictions.summary: Never release a roof rat, it is a non-native species; rehome responsibly.

inquiry_focus: Confirm in writing that Rattus rattus, kept as a captive-bred pet, falls under the Order Rodentia exemption in Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. r. 391-4-8-.05 ('All species except … Rattus rattus …') and therefore needs NO Wild Animal License or permit from DNR to keep, breed, or transfer; and (to the Dept of Agriculture) confirm the pet-dealer threshold for rodents and that pet rodents remain exempt from the import CVI.
